name: LLM-QAT (data-free quantization-aware training, NVIDIA)
bits: w4a4 to w8a8 plus 4-bit KV cache (per-tensor/per-channel groups configured per experiment)
activation_scheme: Quantization-aware training: straight-through estimators over weights AND activations AND the KV cache, with the distillation target being the pretrained model's own greedy/sampled generations rather than any training corpus. This is what makes it 'data-free' and usable on models whose training data is unavailable.
kernels: Research-only. No shipping kernel named in the paper; evaluated with simulation/fake-quant in the paper's harness.
quality_delta: Paper states 'large improvements over training-free methods, especially in the low-bit settings' for LLaMA 7B/13B/30B down to 4-bit. The abstract gives no numeric perplexity delta and the experiments section was not read this session, so no number is recorded here. Third-party comparisons elsewhere cite LLM-QAT trailing W4A4 by ~22 points of zero-shot accuracy, but that figure is from SpinQuant's table, not from this paper.
notes: Enum mismatch, deliberate: the closest existing value is 'ternary' but LLM-QAT is a training regime, not a ternary format - it is reported at 4-bit and above. Request the parent add a 'qat' enum value. The important thing this record captures is the W4A4-vs-W4A16 distinction: LLM-QAT is a genuine W4A4 method (it quantizes activations, unlike GPTQ/AWQ), but its W4A4 has no hardware int4xint4 path - same caveat as QuaRot and SpinQuant. Also note the KV cache is quantized here, which is unusual for a weight-quantization paper and links Task A to Task D.
